agent_claim: OAuth 2.0; broad REST API; buildable now.
human_finding: Accepted. Salesforce documents OAuth 2.0 for REST resources through external client apps. New connected-app creation is restricted from Spring ’26, so the implementation note was updated to prefer external client apps.

agent_claim: OAuth and API-token authentication; broad ticketing APIs.
human_finding: Accepted with a time-sensitive note: OAuth is the recommended route and legacy API tokens are scheduled for deactivation on 30 April 2027.

agent_claim: OAuth 2.0 and broad Web API.
human_finding: Accepted. Slack’s developer platform exposes OAuth-based app installation and a broad Web API surface.

agent_claim: Self-serve OAuth marketing API.
human_finding: Corrected. Marketing permissions use three-legged OAuth, but Advertising API access requires application and approval; some products remain private or require extra qualification.

agent_claim: OAuth with REST and GraphQL Admin APIs.
human_finding: Accepted with correction to emphasis: build on the GraphQL Admin API. The REST Admin API has been legacy since October 2024.

agent_claim: Integrations imply a usable enrichment API.
human_finding: Corrected. No public developer documentation or credential path was evidenced from the supplied company surface. Integrations are not proof of a public API.

agent_claim: Tokens/OAuth; broad REST and GraphQL APIs.
human_finding: Accepted. Fine-grained personal tokens, GitHub Apps, OAuth apps, REST, and GraphQL are documented.

agent_claim: OAuth/public integrations and REST API.
human_finding: Accepted. Public integrations use OAuth; internal integrations use a workspace token. The public REST API is documented.

agent_claim: API keys/OAuth and broad REST APIs.
human_finding: Accepted. Secret and restricted API keys support direct integrations; OAuth is available for Connect platforms.

agent_claim: OAuth-authenticated MCP rather than a conventional public REST surface; product form and plan access were not fully captured.
human_finding: Corrected. Otter is an AI meeting, recording, and transcription application available on Windows, macOS, web, iOS, and Android. The permanent Basic free plan includes the desktop apps, 300 monthly transcription minutes, and the Otter MCP server. Its hosted MCP endpoint uses OAuth with granular permissions and exposes tools to search meetings, fetch transcripts, and retrieve user information. Pro and Business add capacity and collaboration features; the separate Otter API and webhooks are Enterprise features.
access_override: Permanent Basic free plan includes desktop apps and hosted MCP; API and webhooks require Enterprise
description_override: Desktop, web, and mobile AI meeting assistant for recording, transcription, summaries, searchable meeting knowledge, and agent access.
auth_override: OAuth with granular permissions for hosted MCP; no public MCP API key
surface_override: Windows/macOS desktop apps + web/mobile apps + official hosted read-only MCP; API and webhooks on Enterprise
evidence_note: Reviewer supplied Otter's pricing-plan screen and clarified the desktop-app product form; current official pricing lists Otter MCP on the permanent Basic free plan.

agent_claim: MCP was treated as one ambiguous bidirectional Aircall integration surface.
human_finding: Corrected. For AI Actions, the developer hosts an MCP server and Aircall's Voice Agents, Messaging Agents, or AI Assist invoke its tools; publishing that connector requires Technology Partner review. Aircall separately offers a beta read-only MCP server for assistants retrieving call intelligence. REST APIs and webhooks handle system-initiated access and event workflows.

agent_claim: Credential availability was left unclear after automated documentation crawling.
human_finding: Corrected. The live cloud signup flow was manually observed to require billing-card details, so practical access is a card-gated self-serve trial. This contradicts Twenty's current public pricing page, which states that the 30-day trial requires no credit card. Pro includes REST, GraphQL, webhooks, and a native MCP server; self-hosting remains an alternative.
access_override: Self-serve trial — billing card required in observed signup
evidence_note: Live signup observation supplied by reviewer; published pricing page currently contradicts it.

agent_claim: The automated crawl left credential availability unclear.
human_finding: Corrected. Zoho CRM provides a permanent self-serve Free edition that can be used without purchasing a plan, including limited API credits and core CRM tools. Trials of paid editions are optional and temporarily unlock higher-tier features. When a trial ends, users can continue with the Free edition; payment is required only for advanced paid-plan capabilities. The logged-in experience was observed offering 30 days, while official core CRM documentation currently states 15 days and CRM Plus states 30 days.
access_override: Self-serve Free edition — no paid plan required; optional paid-tier trials
evidence_note: Free edition remains usable without payment. Reviewer observed a 30-day paid-tier offer; official core CRM docs state 15 days, while CRM Plus states 30 days.

agent_claim: Automated evidence mixed product access, API access, and MCP signals without a clear product description.
human_finding: Corrected. Devin is an AI software-engineering agent that plans and executes engineering work. Current official pricing includes a $0 individual Free plan with a light agent quota and limited model availability. Cloud-agent and API automation capabilities require paid self-serve or organization access. API v3 uses organization service-user keys with the cog_ prefix; human personal access tokens remain closed beta. Devin also exposes MCP capabilities.
access_override: Self-serve $0 Free plan; paid plan or organization required for API/cloud automation
description_override: AI software-engineering agent that plans, codes, tests, and delivers repository changes.
auth_override: Service-user API key (cog_); human PAT is closed beta
surface_override: Public REST API v3 + Devin MCP

agent_claim: The crawl detected partial CLI/API signals but did not distinguish the three connection and billing models.
human_finding: Corrected. Higgsfield is a generative-media platform with three programmatic routes. MCP connects ChatGPT, Claude, Telegram, and other chat agents through browser/OAuth login with no API key and consumes paid subscription credits. CLI + Skills connects Claude Code and other coding agents through browser login, also using plan credits without an API key. The separate REST API and SDK use a generated API key with the Key authorization scheme and an independently funded prepaid balance; an ordinary Higgsfield subscription is not required for API access. The product also exposes plugins for Photoshop, After Effects, Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve, Figma, Blender, and Minecraft.
access_override: Self-serve, billing required — paid plan credits for MCP/CLI or prepaid balance for API
description_override: Generative-media platform for image, video, audio, characters, and creative workflows.
auth_override: MCP/CLI: browser OAuth login; REST API: API key using Authorization: Key
surface_override: REST API + SDKs + MCP (ChatGPT/Claude/Telegram) + CLI/Skills + creative plugins
evidence_note: Reviewer supplied an in-product connection screen showing ChatGPT, Claude, Claude Code, Telegram, CLI, API, and creative plugins.

agent_claim: The crawl found REST/API signals but did not capture the actual signup payment gate or distinguish private from public integrations.
human_finding: Corrected. HighLevel is a CRM, marketing, communications, and workflow-automation platform. The observed signup flow requires a payment card for a 14-day trial, then charges $97/month for Starter or $297/month for Unlimited. Developers can create private integrations directly using scoped private integration tokens or build OAuth 2.0 apps. Public Marketplace distribution requires app approval. The REST API covers contacts, conversations, messaging, calendars, appointments, payments, and webhooks.
access_override: Self-serve 14-day trial — card required; then $97 Starter or $297 Unlimited monthly
description_override: CRM and marketing automation platform for leads, messaging, appointments, payments, and workflows.
auth_override: OAuth 2.0 or scoped private integration token
surface_override: Broad public REST API + webhooks; public Marketplace apps require approval
evidence_note: Reviewer supplied the live checkout screen showing card entry, 14-day trial, $97/month Starter, and $297/month Unlimited pricing.

agent_claim: The automated crawl detected API authentication but left practical credential access unclear.
human_finding: Corrected. Twilio provides a self-serve 30-day free trial without a credit card. The trial includes limited product-specific units and restrictions such as verified recipients and geographic limits. Production use upgrades to usage-based pay-as-you-go service by adding billing details and an initial balance. Developers can use API keys or Account SID plus Auth Token credentials across Twilio's communications APIs and SDKs.
access_override: Self-serve 30-day free trial — no card; then usage-based pay-as-you-go
description_override: Cloud communications platform for messaging, voice, email, verification, and customer engagement.
auth_override: API key recommended; Account SID + Auth Token via Basic Auth also supported
surface_override: Broad public REST APIs + server SDKs + webhooks

agent_claim: The crawler left Airtable's credential and plan access unclear.
human_finding: Corrected. Airtable offers a permanent self-serve Free plan. A new account's first Free workspace receives a complimentary 14-day Team trial and can return to Free afterward. Team costs $20 per seat monthly when billed annually or $24 monthly; Business costs $45 annually or $54 monthly; Enterprise Scale is custom. The Web API is available on every plan through scoped personal access tokens or OAuth. Free includes 1,000 API calls per workspace per month, Team 100,000, and Business or Enterprise unlimited calls, all subject to five requests per second per base.
access_override: Permanent self-serve Free plan; first workspace gets optional 14-day Team trial
description_override: Collaborative database and application platform for structured data, workflows, and internal tools.
auth_override: Scoped personal access token or OAuth 2.0
surface_override: Public Web API + OAuth integrations + webhooks; API limits vary by plan
evidence_note: Reviewer supplied Airtable's live pricing screen showing Free, Team, Business, and Enterprise Scale tiers.

agent_claim: The initial rules identified OAuth, GraphQL, and MCP but did not clearly establish plan access, alternative credentials, webhook coverage, or MCP permissions.
human_finding: Corrected. Linear has a permanent $0 Free plan, self-serve Basic at $10 per user/month and Business at $16 per user/month when billed yearly, plus a custom annual Enterprise tier. Its public GraphQL API supports queries and mutations using a personal API key or OAuth 2.0, and Linear provides signed webhooks for real-time changes. Linear also hosts an official remote MCP server: the standard endpoint exposes read-write tools for issues, projects, comments, and other objects, while a dedicated endpoint or read OAuth scope provides read-only access. MCP uses interactive OAuth 2.1, or can accept a bearer OAuth token or Linear API key directly.
access_override: Permanent self-serve $0 Free plan; paid Basic and Business tiers; Enterprise is sales-led
description_override: Product-development and issue-tracking platform with projects, roadmaps, workflows, and agent capabilities.
auth_override: Personal API key or OAuth 2.0 for GraphQL; OAuth 2.1, OAuth bearer token, or API key for MCP
surface_override: Broad public GraphQL API + signed webhooks + official hosted read-write/read-only MCP
evidence_note: Reviewer supplied Linear's live pricing screen showing Free, Basic, Business, and Enterprise tiers.

agent_claim: The automated crawl detected API-key and OAuth signals but left the API surface and commercial access unclear.
human_finding: Corrected. Freshdesk offers a six-month Free Program for up to two agents, but the Free plan has zero public API calls and no integration capability. API access starts on the paid Growth plan; the 14-day trial permits 50 API calls per minute. Developers can build and submit paid Freshworks Marketplace apps, with per-agent or per-account monthly pricing. The standard Marketplace revenue split pays the developer 80% of monthly recurring app revenue and Freshworks retains 20%.
access_override: Free developer tooling; customer API usage requires Growth or higher; 14-day trial includes limited API access
description_override: Customer-support platform for ticketing, conversations, contacts, knowledge bases, automation, and marketplace integrations.
auth_override: API key for direct account integrations; OAuth 2.0 for public marketplace apps
surface_override: Broad public REST API + webhooks; paid Marketplace distribution uses an 80/20 developer/Freshworks revenue split
evidence_note: Reviewer flagged the Freshworks Paid Apps Program's 80/20 revenue share; official terms confirm developers receive 80% of MRR.

agent_claim: The supplied documentation URL returned 404, leaving authentication, API surface, access, and buildability unclear.
human_finding: Corrected. Plain is an API-first customer-support platform with a public GraphQL API, webhooks, events, machine users, and native integrations including Slack, Linear, Jira, GitHub, incident tools, CRMs, and AI agents. Plain has no permanent free workspace plan: every workspace begins with a seven-day trial that requires no credit card, then requires a paid Foundation, Horizon, or Frontier subscription. API access is included across the paid plans rather than sold as a separate API add-on.
access_override: Self-serve 7-day free trial with no card; paid subscription required afterward
description_override: API-first B2B customer-support platform for shared channels, customer context, workflows, AI agents, and product integrations.
auth_override: Scoped machine-user API key for GraphQL; OAuth for Plain's hosted MCP server
surface_override: Public GraphQL API + webhooks + events + hosted OAuth MCP + native integrations on paid plans
evidence_note: Reviewer clarified that Plain supports API integrations but does not offer a permanent free plan; current official pricing confirms a seven-day trial followed by paid plans.

agent_claim: The automated crawl found API-key, OAuth, REST, and MCP signals but left practical plan access unclear.
human_finding: Corrected. TranscriptAPI is a hosted YouTube data service covering transcripts, video search, channel search and browsing, playlists, and upload monitoring. New accounts receive 100 free credits without a payment card. Continued use requires the single paid plan: $5 monthly or $54 annually, with 1,000 credits per month. Both REST API and hosted MCP access are included; most successful requests cost one credit, while latest-upload RSS and channel-handle resolution are free.
access_override: Self-serve 100-credit free trial with no card; then $5/month or $54/year
description_override: Hosted YouTube transcript, search, channel, playlist, and upload-monitoring service for applications and AI agents.
auth_override: Bearer API key for REST; OAuth or API key for MCP depending on client
surface_override: Public REST API + hosted MCP + agent skills; API and MCP included on the paid plan
evidence_note: Reviewer supplied the live pricing page; official pricing states 100 free credits without a card and one paid plan with API and MCP access.
